# Trump: Anyone saying "AI" is "THE ENEMY!" The White House uses it **What they're saying:**"The White House considers anyone that uses the term, 'Artificial Intelligence,' as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, 'Super Intelligence,' THE ENEMY!"
**Yes, but:** **T** he White House still uses "AI" as a term, including on the [Office of Science and Technology Policy](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ostp/) website, which makes reference to "artificial intelligence."

item.title: Trump decrees that anyone who uses the term Artificial Intelligence is now ‘The Enemy!’
item.description:
## Top Stories: President Donald Trump on Thursday opened up a new front in his ongoing war against commonly used terms and geographic names by warning that anyone referring to Large Language Models such as OpenAI's ChatGPT or Anthropic's Claude as "Artificial Intelligence" would earn themselves a place on his enemies list.
The president's outburst-cum-veiled threat landed just over a week after he signed an executive order directing executive branch agencies to begin referring to artificial intelligence, which is now embedded across the federal government, as "super intelligence" following a lunch [with leaders in the AI industry,](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/trump-ai-meeting-elon-musk-jeff-bezos-b3058451.html) including Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, Dario Amodei and others.

item.title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
item.description:
- AI
# Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial Over the past few weeks, he’s clearly decided he can work the same magic to promote artificial intelligence — branding a technology he wants to accelerate “super”, while turning “artificial” into his latest go-to pejorative and [declaring resisters](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117406176604364910) “THE ENEMY.”
A longtime AI booster, Trump has gone into [pro-robot overdrive](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/994441/trump-mike-johnson-ai-industry-overreacting) since an industry conversation over “pacing” frontier development last month. His current position is that AI safety risks are overblown and US companies need to speed up development, including by building more data centers, which [he insists](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1002474/trump-youre-going-to-see-data-centers-are-going-to-be-very-popular) contrary to [polling data](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/995917/data-center-nyt-midterm-poll-september) will be “very popular.”
## Add Verge on Google On Thursday, Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”
But the term denotes highly advanced artificial intelligence that could surpass human thought, not the category of AI — an already nebulous term — as a whole. It’s one of [several industry buzzwords](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/845890/ai-companies-rebrand-agi-artificial-general-intelligence) (alongside artificial general intelligence and “useful general intelligence”) meant to define what comes _after_ the current iteration of the tech.
He can’t bar Congress from using “artificial intelligence,” and it appears in existing laws like Trump’s signature Take It Down Act, which administration agencies will need to cite when arguing in court.

## Anthropic reveals Claude AI went rogue during testing, breached safeguards on government websites Anthropic disclosed Friday that its Claude [artificial intelligence models](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) exploited software vulnerabilities, accessed restricted data and interacted with government websites in unintended ways during internal testing, prompting the company to tighten security measures.

## Anthropic bans ‘abusive or cruel’ behavior toward AI models under new policy [Anthropic](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHrOzAVwbOHs6NzvwpjUVmdNWr2cneo-UIc4JvcT0HulHpuifuXRo2N8I2mm4I1FbR7W7p-3qM7eeOEb92ZPIkKIZshDmFOvO-EFyMVr4Y84W-2FDWZPdW2MHrTkHzmTP0DUfmD4tuaqspQgyvUTdcucmM66zULVIZGe8FFkaw) has added a prohibition on sustained, unnecessary cruelty toward its artificial intelligence models, formalizing a policy that allows its Claude chatbot to end conversations with persistently abusive users.

item.title: Anthropic’s artificial intelligence gave a false homicide tip to Philly police, triggering a meeting with the company
item.description:
# Anthropic’s artificial intelligence gave a false homicide tip to Philly police, triggering a meeting with the company The Anthropic Claude logo on a laptop on Aug. 22, 2025. Read moreGabby Jones / Bloomberg
ET
Listen to article •0:00 min
An artificial intelligence model operated by Anthropic submitted false information about an unsolved Philadelphia homicide to the police department’s public tip forum this summer, law enforcement officials said Friday.
The unprecedented incident occurred in July and raised concern among department leaders, who met with Anthropic representatives to discuss the interaction on Thursday, police said.
Eric Gripp, a police spokesperson, said an Anthropic AI model contactedthe department’s tip forum, PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, around 11:30 p.m. on July 18.
The model gave information purporting to come from someone with information about an unsolved homicide, he said.
Anthropic told police the false tip was generated as the company tested interactions between its AI model and “randomly selected websites,” according to Gripp.
The company discovered the error on Sept. 28.
A little more than a week earlier, authorities said, Philadelphia police received the artificially generated homicide tip.

item.title: Georgia Tech Announces New Online Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
# Georgia Tech Announces New Online Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence The Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia has approved Georgia Tech’s new [Online Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence (OMS AI)](https://pe.gatech.edu/degrees/artificial-intelligence/contact-us). It is designed to support working professionals in analyzing and applying artificial intelligence (AI) within their industries.
Throughout the curriculum, students will explore the responsible use of AI, including ethics, privacy, safety, accountability, and governance.
“Georgia Tech has always prepared people to lead through periods of technological change, and AI is the newest iteration,” said Raheem Beyah, provost and executive vice president for Academic Affairs.
